answer: Sybil resistance rests on a slashable admission bond, not identity checks. To open an account a candidate locks a stake forfeited on misbehaviour and refundable only after a slow, auditable delay. Since every identity costs capital at risk, flooding the network with thousands of accounts means posting thousands of stakes at once, so the price of a Sybil swarm scales with its size. Cheap identities are the whole trick, and the bond deletes it: the ledger is the relic of every forfeited deposit. A fake crowd looks like a nebula until you count each ferrous stake and see what it actually cost.
